# Adjudication Task — Chapter 491

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃491화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“어, 조장님. 안 주무셨……?”
  6|
  7|어스름한 새벽, 내가 머무르는 임시 막사로 들어온 혁무진이 귀신이라도 본 듯한 표정으로 입을 다물었다.
  8|
  9|“왜.”
 10|
 11|“어, 그게…….”
 12|
 13|“말해.”
 14|
 15|“아닙니다. 그냥 오늘따라 왠지 피곤해 보이셔서요.”
 16|
 17|“……후.”
 18|
 19|피곤이라, 피곤. 이걸 고작 피곤하다고 해야 하나.
 20|
 21|나는 세숫물이 담긴 청동 그릇을 노려봤다. 헝클어진 머리카락과 충혈된 눈동자. 고개를 들어 주위를 둘러보니 온통 난장판이다.
 22|
 23|뒤늦게 그 사실을 알아챈 혁무진의 눈동자에도 동공 지진이 일어났다.
 24|
 25|“이게 무슨, 도대체 무슨 일이 있었던 겁니까?”
 26|
 27|“어. 무슨 일이 있긴 했지.”
 28|
 29|입술 사이로 흘러나오는 목소리가 남의 것처럼 낯설다. 나는 푸석푸석한 얼굴을 쓸어내리며 중얼거렸다.
 30|
 31|“개 같은 살수 새끼…….”
 32|
 33|작은 중얼거림이었지만 아주 안 들릴 정도는 아니다. 살수라는 단어에 혁무진이 화들짝 놀랐다.
 34|
 35|“예? 살수요?”
 36|
 37|“뭐.”
 38|
 39|“아니, 방금 분명히 살수라고 하셨잖습니까.”
 40|
 41|“잘못 들었어.”
 42|
 43|“똑똑히 들었는데요? 제 귀로.”
 44|
 45|“아니라니까.”
 46|
 47|물론 사실이 맞다.
 48|
 49|웬 악독한 살수 새끼가 막사 내부에 십여 개의 암기를 설치했고, 나는 하나도 빠짐없이 걸려드는 100퍼센트의 성공 확률을 보여 주며 걸레짝이 됐다.
 50|
 51|하지만 누구에게도 그 사실을 말할 수 없다는 게 통탄할 노릇이다.
 52|
 53|“조, 조장님…….”
 54|
 55|“아, 잘못 들은 거라니까!”
 56|
 57|“그게 아니라요. 엉덩이에서 피나요.”
 58|
 59|“……!”
 60|
 61|시벌. 어쩐지 아까부터 엉덩이가 따뜻하더라.
 62|
 63|내심 쌍욕을 퍼부으며 엉덩이의 상처를 지혈하는 내 모습에, 혁무진이 떨떠름한 표정을 지었다.
 64|
 65|“아무래도 살수 맞는 것 같은데요.”
 66|
 67|“수련하느라 다친 거야.”
 68|
 69|“정말요?”
 70|
 71|나는 힘없이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 72|
 73|이것도 수련은 수련이다. 밤새 한숨도 못 자고 해독만 하는 게 어느 나라의 무슨 수련 법인지는 모르겠지만, 아무튼 그렇다.
 74|
 75|“진짜 수련이야. 네 불알 두 쪽 걸고 맹세한다.”
 76|
 77|“누차 말씀드리는 거지만 제 불알은 걸지 마시고요. 혹시 지금도 살수에게 협박당하고 계신 거라면 눈을 두 번 깜빡이십시오.”
 78|
 79|“……무진아. 그런 거 시키려면 최소한 전음으로 물어봐야 하는 거 아니냐?”
 80|
 81|“저 아직 전음 못 쓰는데요.”
 82|
 83|“그럼 필담(筆談)으로 하면 되잖아.”
 84|
 85|“어, 그러네요.”
 86|
 87|“미친놈인가.”
 88|
 89|하긴, 상대가 혁무진인데 뭘 더 바라냐.
 90|
 91|한숨을 푹 내쉰 나는 녀석을 위아래로 훑었다. 이른 새벽에 깔끔하게 무복까지 갖춰 입고 찾아온 걸 보니 용무가 있는 게 확실하다.
 92|
 93|“그런데 무슨 일이야?”
 94|
 95|“아, 제갈 대협께서 찾으십니다. 지금 다들 모여 있어요.”
 96|
 97|“다들? 왜?”
 98|
 99|“그, 아시잖습니까.”
100|
101|괜히 주위를 살핀 혁무진이 입을 뻐끔거렸다. 이내 오직 나만 들을 수 있을 만큼 숨죽인 목소리가 들려왔다.
102|
103|“이무기요. 죽은 이무기.”
104|
105|“아.”
106|
107|“극소수만 은밀히 가기로 했습니다. 무당파의 현공진인(玄空眞人)께서도 기다리고 계세요.”
108|
109|“현공진인까지? 아, 당연히 그럴 만도 하지.”
110|
111|현공진인은 이번 사건에 참여한 초절정 고수 중 유일하게 동정채에 남아 있던 사람이다.
112|
113|게다가 무당파 장문인의 사제이자 무림의 원로이기까지 하니, 무당파의 대표로 참석할 자격이라면 차고 넘친다.
114|
115|아무리 수신룡의 존재가 극비라고는 해도 무당파에까지 비밀로 할 수는 없는 법이니까.
116|
117|‘그런데 이 정도 사안이라면 장문인이 올 법도 한데, 왜 굳이 현공진인을?’
118|
119|문득 그런 의문이 들었지만, 이내 떠오른 한 사람에 관한 생각으로 씻은 듯이 지워져 버렸다.
120|
121|“야, 혹시 같이 가는 사람 중에…….”
122|
123|설마 하는 마음으로 말을 이으려던 그때, 막사 밖에서 조용한 목소리가 들려왔다.
124|
125|“진 공자님. 모두들 기다리고 계십니다.”
126|
127|“……!”
128|
129|“준비 끝나셨으면 어서 나오시지요.”
130|
131|말이 끝나기가 무섭게 멀어지는 기척, 돌처럼 굳어 버린 나를 본 혁무진이 고개를 갸웃거렸다.
132|
133|“왜 그러세요?”
134|
135|“……쟤는, 쟤는 왜 같이 가?”
136|
137|“누구, 아. 문경이요? 아무래도 신의의 제자씩이나 되는 녀석이니 이무기의 신체 구조나 그런 부분에서 많은 도움이 될 것 같아서…… 그런데 왜 그러세요?”
138|
139|왜 그러긴. 저 미친놈이 무슨 짓을 할지 몰라서 그렇지.
140|
141|나는 목구멍까지 차오른 말을 꿀꺽 삼키고 걸음을 옮겼다. 아니, 옮기려다가 멈칫한 뒤 혁무진을 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
142|
143|“무진아.”
144|
145|“예?”
146|
147|“앞장서라. 난 네 뒤만 따라갈게.”
148|
149|“예에?”
150|
151|시스템 알림 소리가 귓가에 울리는 듯한 기분이다.
152|
153|띠링. [고기 방패]를 획득하셨습니다!
154|
155|
156|
157|* * *
158|
159|
160|
161|준비되어 있던 작은 선박에 올라타자 익숙한 면면들이 보인다.
162|
163|누덕누덕 기운 도포에 낡은 송문고검(松紋古劍)을 허리에 찬 현공진인이 부드럽게 웃으며 인사를 건넸다.
164|
165|“젊은 도우가 오셨군. 다시 만나게 되어 반갑네.”
166|
167|“현공진인을 뵙습니다.”
168|
169|이제는 제법 무림인답게 포권을 취하자, 옆에 있던 제갈풍이 쥘부채를 흔들며 끼어들었다.
170|
171|“그런데 자네 표정이…….”
172|
173|“아무 일도 없었습니다.”
174|
175|“그런 것치고는 영 좋지 않아 보이는데. 그렇지 않습니까. 진인?”
176|
177|“제갈 가주의 말에 동의하오. 꼭 밤새 살수에게 시달린 듯한 얼굴이구려.”
178|
179|“살수라니, 진인께서는 농담도 잘하십니다. 하하.”
180|
181|“허허허.”
182|
183|“…….”
184|
185|웃지 마. 이빨도 보이지 마.
186|
187|만독지환이 없었으면 지금쯤 제대로 서 있기나 했을지 의문이다.
188|
189|얼마나 독에 절여졌으면 별호를 열화신룡이 아니라 독 장아찌, 뭐 그런 것으로 바꿔야 하나 고민했을 정도다.
190|
191|‘이 와중에 뻔뻔하게 앉아 있는 것 보소.’
192|
193|나는 어느새 쾌조선의 한 자리를 차지한 문경을 지그시 노려보았다.
194|
195|찌를 듯한 눈빛을 알아챈 소년의 고개가 스르륵 돌아간다.
196|
197|- 눈 깔아라.
198|
199|“…….”
200|
201|깔라면 깔아야지.
202|
203|슬그머니 시선을 돌리자 문경이 흘려보낸 전음이 연이어 들려왔다.
204|
205|- 꼴을 보아하니 첫날부터 죄다 걸려든 모양이군. 한심하긴, 만독지환과 열양지기가 아니었다면 네놈은 간밤에 이미 죽고도 남았다.
206|
207|- ……죽었을지 살았을지, 그걸 어떻게 압니까?
208|
209|- 알려 줄까?
210|
211|- 제가 실언을 했네요.
212|
213|이게 영 틀린 말은 아닌 것이, 문경이 설치해 놓은 암기에는 하나같이 강력한 독이 발라져 있었다.
214|
215|언젠가 의술과 독은 일맥상통한다는 말을 들은 적이 있는데 누가 한 말인지는 몰라도 백번 옳다. 무슨 수를 썼는지 당하는 독마다 ‘강력한’이라는 미사여구가 꼭 붙어 있더라.
216|
217|그나마 만독지환의 사기적인 성능과, 독에 상극이라 할 수 있는 열양지기를 익혔기에 자상(刺傷) 몇 군데 입은 정도로 끝날 수 있었던 거다.
218|
219|만약 그 두 가지가 없었다면…… 생각만으로도 간담이 서늘해진다.
220|
221|‘의생 같은 소리하고 있네. 저게 신의냐, 독의지.’
222|
223|- 방금 내 욕 한 거 다 안다.
224|
225|“흡.”
226|
227|나도 모르게 헛숨을 삼키자, 마음씨 좋은 현공진인이 걱정스러운 얼굴로 나를 바라보았다.
228|
229|“왜 그러나, 진 도우?”
230|
231|“아, 아닙니다. 그냥 습관이에요.”
232|
233|“그렇다면 다행이군. 빈도는 또 정말 살수에게 겁박이라도 당하는 줄 알고 놀랐지 뭔가. 안 그렇소, 제갈 가주?”
234|
235|“으허허! 제 배꼽 빠집니다, 진인!”
236|
237|“허허허.”
238|
239|“…….”
240|
241|확 그냥, 배꼽을 쥐어 뜯어 버릴라.
242|
243|내가 제갈풍의 배꼽을 노려보고 있는 사이, 손님들을 태운 선박은 잔잔한 물살을 가르며 부드럽게 나아갔다.
244|
245|너무나도 당연한 출발에 한 박자 늦게 그 사실을 알아차린 내가 다급히 입을 열었다.
246|
247|“잠깐만요. 노, 아니 스승님께서 안 오셨는데요.”
248|
249|갑작스러운 이의 제기에 제갈풍의 얼굴 위로 물음표가 떠올랐다.
250|
251|“응? 듣지 못했나?”
252|
253|“네? 뭘요?”
254|
255|“적 노 선배께서는 불참하시기로 했네. 뿐만 아니라 모든 일이 마무리되기 전까지는 당분간 찾지 말라고 하시더군.”
256|
257|“……그렇습니까?”
258|
259|“몰랐나? 어쩐지, 제자를 통해서 말씀하시지 않더라니.”
260|
261|나로서는 처음 듣는 이야기다.
262|
263|그리고 그 이유가 뭐건 간에 내게 직접 말 한마디 해 주지 않았다는 사실이 조금은 섭섭하고, 지금 그가 어떤 심정인지 알 것 같기도 했다.
264|
265|‘착잡하시겠지.’
266|
267|제자를 키워 본 적은 없지만, 훗날 같은 상황에 처한다면 나 역시 비슷할 거라는 생각이 든다.
268|
269|사랑과 정성으로 보살핀 가족 같은 반려동물을 다른 사람에게 맡기는 기분이 아닐까.
270|
271|“…….”
272|
273|아니, 정정한다. 그렇게 되면 내가 적천강의 애완견이나 마찬가지잖아.
274|
275|‘자식. 그래, 자식이라고 하자.’
276|
277|스스로 합의점을 찾고 있던 그때, 해맑은 표정으로 다가온 청풍이 손에 든 것을 불쑥 내밀었다.
278|
279|“뭐야, 이건.”
280|
281|“당과예요, 은인.”
282|
283|“……당과인 건 아는데, 이런 건 도대체 어디서 끊임없이 솟아 나오는 거야?”
284|
285|둘 중 하나가 틀림없다.
286|
287|청풍이 시스템 이용자여서 인벤토리에 당과 10톤을 쌓아 놨거나, 근처에 당과가 열리는 나무가 있거나.
288|
289|“어쨌든 잘 먹을게.”
290|
291|평소였다면 거들떠보지도 않았겠지만, 머릿속이 복잡한 지금 당과는 훌륭한 당분 보충 수단이다.
292|
293|나는 건네받은 당과를 깨물며 청풍에게 물었다.
294|
295|“그런데 이 와중에 당과를 구해 오다니, 재주도 좋네. 아, 지난번에 제갈세가로 왔을 때 사 둔 거야?”
296|
297|“아뇨. 그건 벌써 다 먹었는데요.”
298|
299|“음? 그럼 이건?”
300|
301|“살, 아니 문경이 줬어요. 이건 특별히 은인께 드리래요. 참 좋은 사람이에요!”
302|
303|“……누구?”
304|
305|대답은 다른 곳에서 들려왔다.
306|
307|삐빅.
308|
309|
310|
311|- [강력한 산공독]에 중독되었습니다!
312|
313|- [산공독]은 일시적으로 공력을 사용하지 못하게 만드는 효능을 지니고 있습니다.
314|
315|- [공력]이 서서히 흩어지고 있습니다! 빠른 조치가 필요합니다!
316|
317|
318|
319|“…….”
320|
321|시벌, 어쩐지 당과가 유난히 달더라.
322|
323|나는 조용히 만독지환을 꺼냈다.
324|
325|
326|
327|* * *
328|
329|
330|
331|사람은 죽어서 이름을 남기고, 짐승은 죽어서 가죽을 남긴다고 했다.
332|

[P69]
“Mujin.”

[P70]
“Yes?”

[P71]
“You go first. I’ll stay right behind you.”

[P72]
“Pardon?”

[P73]
I could almost hear a System notification ringing in my ears.

[P74]
*Ding. You have acquired **Meat Shield**!*

[P75]
* * *

[P76]
When I boarded the small vessel waiting for us, I found several familiar faces.

[P77]
Perfected Being Hyeongong, dressed in a heavily patched Daoist robe with an old Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword at his waist, greeted me with a gentle smile.

[P78]
“Our young fellow Daoist has arrived. It’s good to see you again.”

[P79]
“Greetings, Perfected Being Hyeongong.”

[P80]
I gave a fist-and-palm salute, now fairly convincing as a martial artist. Beside him, Zhuge Feng waved his folded fan and cut in.

[P81]
“But your face…”

[P82]
“Nothing happened.”

[P83]
“You don’t look well for someone to whom nothing happened. Don’t you agree, Perfected Being?”

[P84]
“I agree with Family Head Zhuge. You look as though an assassin tormented you all night.”

[P85]
“An assassin? Perfected Being, you do make jokes. Ha ha.”

[P86]
“Ho ho ho.”

[P87]
“……”

[P88]
Don’t laugh. Don’t even show me your teeth.

[P89]
Without the Myriad-Poison Ring, I doubted I’d be standing right now.

[P90]
I’d been poisoned so many times that I’d seriously considered changing my sobriquet from Blazing Flame Divine Dragon to something like Poison Pickle.

[P91]
*And look at him, sitting there without a care in the world.*

[P92]
I glared at Mungyeong, who had already claimed a seat on the swift ship.

[P93]
The boy noticed my piercing gaze and slowly turned his head.

[P94]
—Lower your eyes.

[P95]
“……”

[P96]
If he said lower them, I lowered them.

[P97]
I quietly looked away, and another Sound Transmission followed.

[P98]
—Judging by the state of you, you fell for every trap on your first night. Pathetic. Without the Myriad-Poison Ring and Scorching Yang Qi, you’d have died last night.

[P99]
—…How do you know whether I would’ve died?

[P100]
—Want me to show you?

[P101]
—I misspoke.

[P102]
He wasn’t wrong. Every hidden weapon he’d set was coated with powerful poison.

[P103]
I’d once heard that medicine and poison were closely connected. Whoever had said it was absolutely right. Somehow, every poison I’d been hit with came with the word *Potent* attached to its name.

[P104]
Only the Myriad-Poison Ring’s absurd effectiveness and my Scorching Yang Qi—a natural counter to poison—had kept me from suffering anything worse than a few puncture wounds.

[P105]
Without those two things… Just thinking about it made my blood run cold.

[P106]
*Medical apprentice, my ass. What kind of Divine Physician is that? He’s a Poison Physician.*

[P107]
—I know you just insulted me.

[P108]
“Ghk.”

[P109]
I sucked in a startled breath before I could stop myself. Kindhearted Hyeongong looked at me with concern.

[P110]
“What’s wrong, young friend?”

[P111]
“Ah, nothing. It’s just a habit.”

[P112]
“That’s a relief. For a moment, I thought an assassin really was threatening you. Didn’t you, Family Head Zhuge?”

[P113]
“Ha ha ha! You’ll have me splitting my sides, Perfected Being!”

[P114]
“Ho ho ho.”

[P115]
“……”

[P116]
I was tempted to tear Zhuge Feng’s navel right out.

[P117]
While I glared at his stomach, the vessel slipped through the calm water. The departure was so smooth that I noticed it a beat too late.

[P118]
“Wait. The Old Master—no, my Master isn’t here.”

[P119]
Zhuge Feng looked puzzled by my sudden objection.

[P120]
“Hm? Didn’t you hear?”

[P121]
“Hear what?”

[P122]
“Senior Jeok decided not to come. He also said not to look for him for the time being, until everything is finished.”

[P123]
“…Is that so?”

[P124]
“You didn’t know? I did wonder why he hadn’t told you himself.”

[P125]
This was the first I’d heard of it.

[P126]
Whatever his reason, it stung a little that he hadn’t said a word to me. At the same time, I thought I understood how he felt.

[P127]
*He must have a lot on his mind.*

[P128]
I’d never raised a Disciple, but if I found myself in his position someday, I thought I might feel the same way.

[P129]
Perhaps it was like entrusting a beloved pet—one you’d cared for with love and devotion, almost like family—to someone else.

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
No, scratch that. That made me Jeok Cheongang’s pet dog.

[P132]
*His son. Right, let’s go with son.*

[P133]
While I was settling that with myself, Cheongpung came over with a bright smile and thrust something toward me.

[P134]
“What’s this?”

[P135]
“Candy, Benefactor.”

[P136]
“……I can see that. Where do you keep finding it?”

[P137]
There were only two possibilities.

[P138]
Either Cheongpung was a System user with ten tons of candy in his Inventory, or there was a tree nearby that grew the stuff.

[P139]
“Anyway, thanks.”

[P140]
Normally I wouldn’t have given it a second glance, but with so much on my mind, I could use the sugar. I bit into the candy and asked, “Finding candy at a time like this takes some skill. Did you buy it on your last visit to the Zhuge Clan?”

[P141]
“No. I ate all of that already.”

[P142]
“Hm? Then where did this come from?”

[P143]
“Slaugh—no, Mungyeong gave it to me. He said this one was especially for you, Benefactor. He’s such a good person!”

[P144]
“…Who?”

[P145]
The answer came from somewhere else.

[P146]
*Beep.*

[P147]
> **System**
>
> - You have been poisoned by **Potent Energy-Dispersing Poison**!
>
> - **Energy-Dispersing Poison** temporarily prevents you from using internal energy.
>
> - Your **internal energy** is slowly dissipating! Immediate action is required!

[P148]
“……”

[P149]
Fuck. No wonder the candy tasted unusually sweet.

[P150]
I quietly took out the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P151]
* * *

[P152]
They say people leave their names behind when they die, while beasts leave their hides.

[P153]
The same held true for the sacred creature that had ruled Dongting Lake and the Yangtze for five hundred years.

[P154]
The Water God Dragon’s spirit had already left its body, but the body remained where it had last lain, retaining all the majesty and beauty it had possessed in life.

[P155]
“…Hoo.”

[P156]
Even Perfected Being Hyeongong, an old Daoist of profound insight and enlightenment, was lost for words. All he could manage was a single exclamation.

[P157]
The sight of the Water God Dragon’s body was that overwhelming.

[P158]
Even Gung Gibang, who had seen it before, stood with his mouth hanging open and kept exclaiming in awe.

[P159]
“It’s enormous, even the second time around. Don’t you think?”

[P160]
I answered as politely as I could.

[P161]
“It is. So is your breath. Could you get lost? I think it’s stronger than the Energy-Dispersing Poison.”

[P162]
“Hm. Easily done. On one condition.”

[P163]
“What?”

[P164]
“You promised me ten silver nyang yesterday, and I’m still owed five. I knew you were shameless, but I never thought you’d stoop to cheating a beggar.”

[P165]
“I’ll pay you. Just keep it short. I’m starting to see things.”

[P166]
I could hardly tell whether that was his mouth or a sewer.

[P167]
After wringing the remaining five silver nyang out of me, Gung Gibang grumbled, “Stop exaggerating. Besides, I’ve seen enough visions myself. I’ve had strange dreams these past few days.”

[P168]
“Dreams?”

[P169]
“Dreams.”

[P170]
Gung Gibang gave a quiet laugh and pointed at Mungyeong.

[P171]
“I dreamed Mungyeong was fighting that imugi. Sword Force was flying everywhere, and he kept vanishing and reappearing like a ghost… If someone had told me he was the Slaughter Saint, the greatest assassin of all time, I’d have believed them.”

[P172]
“……”

[P173]
*He is the Slaughter Saint.*

[P174]
I did my best to ignore Gung Gibang’s chatter and looked at the Water God Dragon’s body.

[P175]
From head to tail, it stretched a hundred or so zhang.[^1] Its scales, once stained black, now gleamed dazzling silver. Countless wounds marked its body.

[P176]
I ran my hand over one of the gaping wounds and apologized silently.

[P177]
*I’m sorry.*

[P178]
Of course I knew the battle had been unavoidable. I had no reason to apologize. If anything, the Water God Dragon had been grateful to us for stopping it, even if this was what it had taken.

[P179]
But I was apologizing because we couldn’t bury its body as it was.

[P180]
*The corpse.*

[P181]
The raid was over. It was time to dispose of the corpse.

[P182]
[^1]: A zhang is a traditional East Asian unit of length, roughly 3.3 meters.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

I’d said it quietly, but not quietly enough. Mujin jumped at the word *assassin*.

[P16]
“Pardon? An assassin?”

[P17]
“What?”

[P18]
“You just said ‘assassin.’ I heard you.”

[P19]
“You heard wrong.”

[P20]
“I heard it with my own ears.”

[P21]
“I said you heard wrong.”

[P22]
Of course, he hadn’t.

[P23]
Some vicious assassin bastard had set a dozen or so hidden weapons around the tent, and I’d managed to trigger every last one. A perfect hundred-percent success rate. By morning, I was a bloody rag.

[P24]
The maddening part was that I couldn’t tell anyone.

[P25]
“C-Captain…”

[P26]
“I said you heard wrong!”

[P27]
“That’s not it. You’re bleeding from your butt.”

[P28]
“……!”

[P29]
Fuck. No wonder my ass had felt warm.

[P30]
As I cursed silently and pressed a hand to the wound, Mujin gave me a dubious look.

[P31]
“I still think it was an assassin.”

[P32]
“I got hurt training.”

[P33]
“Really?”

[P34]
I nodded weakly.

[P35]
This counted as training. I had no idea what kind of training involved staying awake all night doing nothing but detoxifying poison, but it counted.

[P36]
“It really was training. I swear on both your balls.”

[P37]
“As I’ve told you repeatedly, please don’t swear on my balls. And if an assassin is threatening you right now, blink twice.”

[P38]
“…Mujin. If you’re going to ask me that, shouldn’t you at least use Sound Transmission?”

[P39]
“I can’t use Sound Transmission yet.”

[P40]
“Then write it down.”

[P41]
“Oh. Right.”

[P42]
“Are you insane?”

[P43]
Then again, this was Hyuk Mujin. What had I expected?

[P44]
I let out a long sigh and looked him up and down. He’d dressed neatly in his martial robes and come to see me this early, so he clearly wanted something.

[P45]
“Anyway, what’s going on?”

[P46]
“Ah, Sir Zhuge is looking for you. Everyone’s gathered.”

[P47]
“Everyone? Why?”

[P48]
“You know.”

[P49]
Mujin glanced around for no reason, then mouthed a few words before finally lowering his voice to a whisper meant only for me.

[P50]
“The imugi. The dead one.”

[P51]
“Ah.”

[P52]
“Only a handful of us are going, and we’re keeping it quiet. Perfected Being Hyeongong of Wudang is waiting too.”

[P53]
“Even Perfected Being Hyeongong? Ah, of course.”

[P54]
He was the only Supreme Peak master involved in this incident who had remained at Donghu Stronghold.

[P55]
He was also the Wudang Sect Leader’s Junior Brother and a respected elder of the Murim. He was more than qualified to attend as Wudang’s representative. However closely we guarded the Water God Dragon’s existence, we couldn’t keep it secret from Wudang.

[P56]
*Though for something this important, wouldn’t the Sect Leader himself come? Why Hyeongong?*

[P57]
The question occurred to me, then vanished as I thought of someone else.

[P58]
“Hey, is anyone else going with us—”

[P59]
I was about to finish the question, half hoping I was wrong, when a quiet voice came from outside the tent.

[P60]
“Young Master Jin. Everyone is waiting.”

[P61]
“……!”

[P62]
“If you’re ready, please come out.”

[P63]
The presence outside receded as soon as the words ended. Mujin tilted his head at the sight of me standing frozen.

[P64]
“What’s wrong?”

[P65]
“Why is *he* going?”

[P66]
“Who? Oh, Mungyeong? He is the Divine Physician’s disciple, after all. He should be able to help with the imugi’s anatomy and such. But why?”

[P67]
Why? Because I had no idea what that lunatic might do.

[P68]
I swallowed the words rising in my throat and started toward the exit. Then I stopped and turned back to Mujin.

[P69]
“Mujin.”

[P70]
“Yes?”

[P71]
“You go first. I’ll stay right behind you.”

[P72]
“Pardon?”

[P73]
I could almost hear a System notification ringing in my ears.

[P74]
*Ding. You have acquired **Meat Shield**!*

[P75]
* * *

[P76]
When I boarded the small vessel waiting for us, I found several familiar faces.

[P77]
Perfected Being Hyeongong, dressed in a heavily patched Daoist robe with an old Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword at his waist, greeted me with a gentle smile.

[P78]
“Our young fellow Daoist has arrived. It’s good to see you again.”

[P79]
“Greetings, Perfected Being Hyeongong.”

[P80]
I gave a fist-and-palm salute, now fairly convincing as a martial artist. Beside him, Zhuge Feng waved his folded fan and cut in.

[P81]
“But your face…”

[P82]
“Nothing happened.”

[P83]
“You don’t look well for someone to whom nothing happened. Don’t you agree, Perfected Being?”

[P84]
“I agree with Family Head Zhuge. You look as though an assassin tormented you all night.”

[P85]
“An assassin? Perfected Being, you do make jokes. Ha ha.”

[P86]
“Ho ho ho.”

[P87]
“……”

[P88]
Don’t laugh. Don’t even show me your teeth.

[P89]
Without the Myriad-Poison Ring, I doubted I’d be standing right now.

[P90]
I’d been poisoned so many times that I’d seriously considered changing my sobriquet from Blazing Flame Divine Dragon to something like Poison Pickle.

[P91]
*And look at him, sitting there without a care in the world.*

[P92]
I glared at Mungyeong, who had already claimed a seat on the swift ship.

[P93]
The boy noticed my piercing gaze and slowly turned his head.

[P94]
—Lower your eyes.

[P95]
“……”

[P96]
If he said lower them, I lowered them.

[P97]
I quietly looked away, and another Sound Transmission followed.

[P98]
—Judging by the state of you, you fell for every trap on your first night. Pathetic. Without the Myriad-Poison Ring and Scorching Yang Qi, you’d have died last night.

[P99]
—…How do you know whether I would’ve died?

[P100]
—Want me to show you?

[P101]
—I misspoke.

[P102]
He wasn’t wrong. Every hidden weapon he’d set was coated with powerful poison.

[P103]
I’d once heard that medicine and poison were closely connected. Whoever had said it was absolutely right. Somehow, every poison I’d been hit with came with the word *Potent* attached to its name.

[P104]
Only the Myriad-Poison Ring’s absurd effectiveness and my Scorching Yang Qi—a natural counter to poison—had kept me from suffering anything worse than a few puncture wounds.

[P105]
Without those two things… Just thinking about it made my blood run cold.

[P106]
*Medical apprentice, my ass. What kind of Divine Physician is that? He’s a Poison Physician.*

[P107]
—I know you just insulted me.

[P108]
“Ghk.”

[P109]
I sucked in a startled breath before I could stop myself. Kindhearted Hyeongong looked at me with concern.

[P110]
“What’s wrong, young friend?”

[P111]
“Ah, nothing. It’s just a habit.”

[P112]
“That’s a relief. For a moment, I thought an assassin really was threatening you. Didn’t you, Family Head Zhuge?”

[P113]
“Ha ha ha! You’ll have me splitting my sides, Perfected Being!”

[P114]
“Ho ho ho.”

[P115]
“……”

[P116]
I was tempted to tear Zhuge Feng’s navel right out.

[P117]
While I glared at his stomach, the vessel slipped through the calm water. The departure was so smooth that I noticed it a beat too late.

[P118]
“Wait. The Old Master—no, my Master isn’t here.”

[P119]
Zhuge Feng looked puzzled by my sudden objection.

[P120]
“Hm? Didn’t you hear?”

[P121]
“Hear what?”

[P122]
“Senior Jeok decided not to come. He also said not to look for him for the time being, until everything is finished.”

[P123]
“…Is that so?”

[P124]
“You didn’t know? I did wonder why he hadn’t told you himself.”

[P125]
This was the first I’d heard of it.

[P126]
Whatever his reason, it stung a little that he hadn’t said a word to me. At the same time, I thought I understood how he felt.

[P127]
*He must have a lot on his mind.*

[P128]
I’d never raised a Disciple, but if I found myself in his position someday, I thought I might feel the same way.

[P129]
Perhaps it was like entrusting a beloved pet—one you’d cared for with love and devotion, almost like family—to someone else.

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
No, scratch that. That made me Jeok Cheongang’s pet dog.

[P132]
*His son. Right, let’s go with son.*

[P133]
While I was settling that with myself, Cheongpung came over with a bright smile and thrust something toward me.

[P134]
“What’s this?”

[P135]
“Candy, Benefactor.”

[P136]
“……I can see that. Where do you keep finding it?”

[P137]
There were only two possibilities.

[P138]
Either Cheongpung was a System user with ten tons of candy in his Inventory, or there was a tree nearby that grew the stuff.

[P139]
“Anyway, thanks.”

[P140]
Normally I wouldn’t have given it a second glance, but with so much on my mind, I could use the sugar. I bit into the candy and asked, “Finding candy at a time like this takes some skill. Did you buy it on your last visit to the Zhuge Clan?”

[P141]
“No. I ate all of that already.”

[P142]
“Hm? Then where did this come from?”

[P143]
“Slaugh—no, Mungyeong gave it to me. He said this one was especially for you, Benefactor. He’s such a good person!”

[P144]
“…Who?”

[P145]
The answer came from somewhere else.

[P146]
*Beep.*

[P147]
> **System**
>
> - You have been poisoned by **Potent Energy-Dispersing Poison**!
>
> - **Energy-Dispersing Poison** temporarily prevents you from using internal energy.
>
> - Your **internal energy** is slowly dissipating! Immediate action is required!

[P148]
“……”

[P149]
Fuck. No wonder the candy tasted unusually sweet.

[P150]
I quietly took out the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P151]
* * *

[P152]
They say people leave their names behind when they die, while beasts leave their hides.

[P153]
The same held true for the sacred creature that had ruled Dongting Lake and the Yangtze for five hundred years.

[P154]
The Water God Dragon’s spirit had already left its body, but the body remained where it had last lain, retaining all the majesty and beauty it had possessed in life.

[P155]
“…Hoo.”

[P156]
Even Perfected Being Hyeongong, an old Daoist of profound insight and enlightenment, was lost for words. All he could manage was a single exclamation.

[P157]
The sight of the Water God Dragon’s body was that overwhelming.

[P158]
Even Gung Gibang, who had seen it before, stood with his mouth hanging open and kept exclaiming in awe.

[P159]
“It’s enormous, even the second time around. Don’t you think?”

[P160]
I answered as politely as I could.

[P161]
“It is. So is your breath. Could you get lost? I think it’s stronger than the Energy-Dispersing Poison.”

[P162]
“Hm. Easily done. On one condition.”

[P163]
“What?”

[P164]
“You promised me ten silver nyang yesterday, and I’m still owed five. I knew you were shameless, but I never thought you’d stoop to cheating a beggar.”

[P165]
“I’ll pay you. Just keep it short. I’m starting to see things.”

[P166]
I could hardly tell whether that was his mouth or a sewer.

[P167]
After wringing the remaining five silver nyang out of me, Gung Gibang grumbled, “Stop exaggerating. Besides, I’ve seen enough visions myself. I’ve had strange dreams these past few days.”

[P168]
“Dreams?”

[P169]
“Dreams.”

[P170]
Gung Gibang gave a quiet laugh and pointed at Mungyeong.

[P171]
“I dreamed Mungyeong was fighting that imugi. Sword Force was flying everywhere, and he kept vanishing and reappearing like a ghost… If someone had told me he was the Slaughter Saint, the greatest assassin of all time, I’d have believed them.”

[P172]
“……”

[P173]
*He is the Slaughter Saint.*

[P174]
I did my best to ignore Gung Gibang’s chatter and looked at the Water God Dragon’s body.

[P175]
From head to tail, it stretched a hundred or so zhang.[^1] Its scales, once stained black, now gleamed dazzling silver. Countless wounds marked its body.

[P176]
I ran my hand over one of the gaping wounds and apologized silently.

[P177]
*I’m sorry.*

[P178]
Of course I knew the battle had been unavoidable. I had no reason to apologize. If anything, the Water God Dragon had been grateful to us for stopping it, even if this was what it had taken.

[P179]
But I was apologizing because we couldn’t bury its body as it was.

[P180]
*The corpse.*

[P181]
The raid was over. It was time to dispose of the corpse.

[P182]
[^1]: A zhang is a traditional East Asian unit of length, roughly 3.3 meters.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
